drafts.lead: Dmitri Kanounnikov, Bicycle BI — wants website, 2-3 examples for BI/data firms, how we identify companies modernising reporting, and what 10-30 introductions means
drafts.body:
Dmitri,

Good questions, taking them in order.

Website: koldify.io. The results section is the fastest read: https://koldify.io/#results

Examples. Our track record is in adjacent categories rather than BI and data services specifically, so I am not going to hand you a case study from a different sector and pretend it maps one to one. The mechanics do transfer, and that is the part worth your time. Happy to walk you through exactly how on the call, using real campaigns.

Identifying companies modernising their reporting. Nobody announces it, so we work from signals that reliably precede it: hiring for analytics or data engineering roles, recent moves onto a cloud warehouse, headcount and funding stage, whether anyone owns data internally. That builds the list. The email then does the qualifying, because the companies actually in the middle of a migration are the ones who write back.

10 to 30 introductions means replies from interested people landing in your inbox over a month. Conversations started, not meetings held. Worth being precise about that up front.

If that is useful:

• Monday, August 17 at 1:30 PM EDT
• Tuesday, August 18 at 1:30 PM EDT
• Wednesday, August 19 at 1:30 PM EDT

Madison

drafts.lead: John Enloe, Eagle 5 Energy — asked what our relationship to accredited investors is and whether we already have those relationships
drafts.body:
John,

Worth being precise, because the distinction matters.

We are not placing you in front of a rolodex we already own, and we are not brokers. We build the channel: target list, separate sending infrastructure, outreach in your name, and the people who are interested reply directly to you. The relationship is yours from the first message rather than rented from us, which is deliberate, because introductions that run through a middleman tend to come with a claim on the outcome. We take nothing on capital raised.

Our work in energy is adjacent rather than identical, so I will not overstate it. The mechanics are the same wherever we run them, and I would rather show you how on a call than describe it here.

One practical note. Outreach to accredited investors about oil and gas participations touches solicitation rules, so we would want your counsel comfortable with the copy before anything goes out. Plenty of operators use this for partner and JV outreach for that reason, which is often the better first campaign anyway.

• Monday, August 17 at 2:00 PM EDT
• Tuesday, August 18 at 2:00 PM EDT

Tracy

drafts.lead: Sam, Trochi Data — asked whether all those brokers are greater than $100m in gross revenue
drafts.body:
Sam,

Not by default, and I would rather answer that properly than nod along.

We build the list to the bar you set. If the floor is 100 million gross revenue, that becomes the filter. The thing to know is that revenue figures for private brokerages are not reliably published, so we triangulate from headcount, carrier count, load volume indicators and filings where they exist. That gets you a list that holds up, and anyone promising a certified revenue floor on private brokerages is selling you confidence they do not have.

At that bar the universe is smaller and the targeting has to be sharper, which usually makes the campaign better rather than worse. I can show you how we build and verify that list on the call.

• Monday, August 17 at 1:30 PM EDT
• Wednesday, August 19 at 2:00 PM EDT

Margaret

Praneeth,

Flat monthly retainer. Not per lead, not per meeting, and no percentage of anything you close.

The number moves with scope, so tell me roughly the scale you have in mind and I will put a figure in writing before we speak. Otherwise we can size it on the call in twenty minutes.

• Monday, August 17 at 2:00 PM EDT
• Tuesday, August 18 at 2:00 PM EDT
• Wednesday, August 19 at 1:30 PM EDT

Allison
